purpose: Teach: 王道/東京タワー/大相撲/バッター/金メダル/声優/ジョギング/レア

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さん、本気で、絶対、王道、絶対、の、絶対、商売、絶対、貫いたぞ、覚えてる?本気で
lines.en: Gran — do you remember? When you were younger, your father really committed himself to the traditional path. So sincere about it.
lines.style: Gentle, nostalgic opening. Warm but reaching back into memory. Measured pace. Soft curiosity at the end, as if asking her to travel back with him.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: うん。若い頃、お祖父ちゃん、本気で、絶対、東京タワー、絶対、お連れくださったわよね、覚えてる、あなた?本気で
lines.en: Yes, I do remember. When you were younger, your grandfather really did take me to Tokyo Tower. Don't you remember, dear?
lines.style: Engaged, affectionate. Bright with the pleasure of shared memory. Slight lift at 'Tokyo Tower.' Warm confirmation, not correction. Intimate address on 'dear.'

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 若い頃、ばあさん、本気で、絶対、大相撲、絶対、テレビ、絶対、応援してたわよな、覚えてる?本気で
lines.en: Gran, when you were younger you really were so devoted to watching sumo on the television. You remember that, don't you?
lines.style: Tender, searching. Each memory offered like a small gift. Slight pause before 'sumo'—letting her land on it. The question at the end is gentle, almost hopeful.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: 若い頃、お祖父ちゃん、本気で、絶対、野球の、絶対、バッター、絶対、お好きだったわよね、覚えてる、あなた?本気で
lines.en: Your grandfather really did love baseball players so much back then, didn't he? You remember that about him, I'm sure.
lines.style: Warm recollection, affectionate teasing underlying the words. Slight emphasis on 'baseball players.' Confident, intimate tone—she knows he'll remember. Small smile in the voice.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 若い頃、ばあさん、本気で、絶対、オリンピックの、絶対、金メダル、絶対、選手、絶対、喜んだわよな、覚えてる?本気で
lines.en: Gran, when you were younger you were so genuinely excited when the Olympic gold medalists would win. You remember celebrating like that?
lines.style: Nostalgic, with gentle warmth. Opening soft. The memory of her joy makes his voice lift slightly on 'win.' Tender question at the end.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: 若い頃、お祖父ちゃん、本気で、絶対、ラジオの、絶対、声優、絶対、お好きだったわよね、覚えてる、あなた?本気で
lines.en: Your grandfather really did love those radio voice actors so much, didn't he? You must remember how he enjoyed listening to them.
lines.style: Engaging and sure. Slight brightness on 'voice actors'—a detail she treasures. Warm certainty in the statement. Intimate, confident rhythm.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 若い頃、ばあさん、本気で、絶対、お父さんと、絶対、ジョギング、絶対、なさったわよな、覚えてる?本気で
lines.en: Gran, when you were younger, you and your father really would go jogging together. You remember those times, don't you?
lines.style: Wistful opening. Voice settles into the image of them moving together. Slow, reflective pace. The question is tender—giving her permission to hold onto the memory.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: 若い頃、お祖父ちゃん、本気で、絶対、レア、絶対、なお切手、絶対、集めていらしたわよね、覚えてる、あなた?本気で
lines.en: Your grandfather was really so fond of collecting those rare stamps back then. You do remember that about him, dear?
lines.style: Soft, affectionate certainty. Gentle weight on 'rare stamps'—honoring the specificity. Warm, intimate close. The final question is tender permission to agree, not challenge.
